filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
about: An all-maduro cigar Drew Estate made with Metallica's James Hetfield and Blackened Whiskey distiller Rob Dietrich. The M stands for Metallica and 81 for 1981, the year the band formed.
notes: Drew Estate lists the body as medium to full. Famous Smoke and Neptune rate the strength full, while halfwheel's review found it medium-plus. A Flying Pig, 4 x 32 tins and a 2025 Lancero also exist outside the four core sizes.
verifyNotes: Flavors: removed espresso and leather, which appear only in customer reviews, and used black pepper (Drew Estate) and earth (halfwheel review) instead. Strength Full confirmed on Famous Smoke and on https://www.neptunecigar.com/blackened-cigar; Drew Estate publishes body only, not strength. The 2025 Lancero is confirmed in https://halfwheel.com/blackened-cigars-by-drew-estate-s84-shade-to-black-lancero/465072/.

filler: Nicaragua, USA (Pennsylvania Green River One Sucker)
about: The second Blackened cigar from Drew Estate and Metallica's James Hetfield, putting a Connecticut Shade wrapper over the same maduro binder and filler as the M81. The name plays on the song Fade to Black from the band's 1984 album.
notes: Drew Estate's site calls it simply Blackened S84. A 7 x 40 Lancero was added in September 2025.

about: A Connecticut Shade cigar from Drew Estate that uses Florida Sun Grown filler from Jeff Borysiewicz's 20 acre farm in Clermont, Florida. It is the company's second line built around that tobacco.
notes: Sources disagree on the binder: Drew Estate's site says Connecticut River Valley Habano, while halfwheel and Corona Cigar say Honduran Habano. halfwheel lists the Robusto at 5 1/2 inches; Drew Estate says 5 1/4.

about: Known as FSG, this is Drew Estate's first cigar to use tobacco grown on Jeff Borysiewicz's farm in Clermont, Florida. It began in 2016 as a Corona Cigar Co. exclusive and went national in 2017.
notes: Since January 2022 it has been sold only through Corona Cigar Co. Sources disagree on the wrapper: halfwheel says Brazilian Mata Fina, Corona says Brazilian Arapiraca maduro. Corona rates it medium to full; halfwheel's review found medium to medium-full. The Limited Edition Toro is a different, broadleaf-wrapped blend.

Notes: dropped the Cigar Dojo strength claim, which I could not find. Drew Estate's 2016 launch release says only 'Brazilian wrapper', so Mata Fina rests on halfwheel alone.

wrapperLeaf: Three versions: Brazilian Maduro, Ecuadorian Connecticut Shade, or Cuban-seed Corojo
about: Drew Estate's first brand, started in New York City in 1996 and later moved to Nicaragua. It was a budget, mixed-filler cigar sold in three wrapper versions until Drew Estate dropped the whole line in 2022.
notes: Discontinued in September 2022. It came in three wrappers, so there is no single wrapper type: Neptune rates the Connecticut Shade mild and the Brazilian Maduro and Corojo medium. Blend details come from a retailer, not the maker.

wrapperLeaf: Kentucky fire-cured, barrel-fermented tapa negra over an Indonesian base wrapper
about: A Drew Estate collaboration with Pappy & Company, the Van Winkle family's merchandise business. It is built around Kentucky fire-cured tobacco that is fermented in bourbon barrels, which gives it a smoky, charred oak character.
notes: Blend here is from Drew Estate's site. halfwheel lists a Mexican San Andres base wrapper and a Nicaraguan binder, and the Toro as 6 x 52. Drew Estate says the tobacco ferments in retired Pappy Van Winkle bourbon barrels; halfwheel reported in 2019 that the barrels had not held Pappy, so do not promise it. Made in small batches.
verifyNotes: Notes: the old note said the barrels did not hold Pappy bourbon and credited the halfwheel review, which does not say that. Strength Medium was confirmed on https://www.neptunecigar.com/pappy-van-winkle-cigar; Drew Estate publishes body (Medium) only. The wrapper category is a judgment call: Neptune lists the wrapper color as Maduro.

about: The original Java, a coffee and cocoa infused cigar that Drew Estate makes for Rocky Patel. Most sizes are box-pressed.
notes: Banded Java by Drew Estate; Drew Estate makes it for Rocky Patel, which distributes it. It is an infused (flavored) cigar. Blend comes from retailers, not the maker. Not every size is still stocked by retailers.
